tier2.text: The small intestine is the body's main digestive organ, where most digestion and nearly all absorption, the uptake of nutrients by cells, take place. This hollow organ runs from the stomach to the large intestine. The small intestine is a coiled tube with three regions: the duodenum next to the stomach, then the jejunum, then the ileum. The lining of the small intestine is covered with villi (singular, villus), small hairlike projections that give the lining a furry texture. The absorptive cells of the lining have microvilli, tiny projections of the cell membrane. Enzymes, proteins that speed up chemical reactions, are fixed to the microvilli and finish digesting carbohydrates and proteins. Together with circular folds, which are deep folds in the lining, the villi and microvilli increase the absorbing surface more than 600-fold. Each villus contains a bed of tiny blood vessels and a lymph vessel called a lacteal. Sugars and amino acids from digested carbohydrates and proteins enter the blood directly, but fat breakdown products enter the lacteals. In segmentation, sections of the intestine contract and relax in turn, mixing food with digestive juices and pressing it against the lining for absorption.

quotes.quote: Within the circular folds are small (0.5–1 mm long) hairlike vascularized projections called villi (singular = villus) that give the mucosa a furry texture.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: microvillus: small projection of the plasma membrane of the absorptive cells of the small intestinal mucosa

quotes.quote: Fixed to the surface of the microvilli membranes are enzymes that finish digesting carbohydrates and proteins.

quotes.quote: An enzyme is a catalytic protein that speeds up chemical reactions in the human body.

quotes.quote: These features, which increase the absorptive surface area of the small intestine more than 600-fold, include circular folds, villi, and microvilli

sentences.text: Each villus contains a bed of tiny blood vessels and a lymph vessel called a lacteal.

quotes.quote: each villus contains a capillary bed composed of one arteriole and one venule, as well as a lymphatic capillary called a lacteal.

sentences.text: Sugars and amino acids from digested carbohydrates and proteins enter the blood directly, but fat breakdown products enter the lacteals.

quotes.quote: The breakdown products of carbohydrates and proteins (sugars and amino acids) can enter the bloodstream directly, but lipid breakdown products are absorbed by the lacteals and transported to the bloodstream via the lymphatic system.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: In segmentation, sections of the intestine contract and relax in turn, mixing food with digestive juices and pressing it against the lining for absorption.

quotes.quote: Segmentation in the small intestine does not force chyme through the tract. Instead, it combines the chyme with digestive juices and pushes food particles against the mucosa to be absorbed.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: segmentation: alternating contractions and relaxations of non-adjacent segments of the intestine that move food forward and backward, breaking it apart and mixing it with digestive juices
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
